rules.statement: When a caller needs a filtered subset of a store's entities, add an intent-named query method to the store interface that pushes the filter to the database, instead of paging or listing the whole set and filtering the results in memory.
rules.why: Fetch-all-then-filter-in-memory can't use indexes. It transfers every row and its expensive child collections only to throw most of them away, and the waste compounds when several readers re-scan the same set.
rules.check: Look for code that calls GetPageAsync or a list/get-all store read and then applies Where/filters or loops over the results by enabled flag, id, ownership or similar predicates.

rules.statement: Use generic paging methods on a store (such as GetPageAsync) only for genuinely unfiltered pagination, such as management list endpoints, and never as a way to filter.
rules.why: Paging is not a filtering mechanism. Filtered reads should be discrete, index-friendly queries.
rules.check: Flag new runtime readers that page through a whole store to find matching entities.

rules.statement: Keep store and persistence abstractions ORM-agnostic: do not expose IQueryable, Expression<Func<...>> predicates or specification objects on store interfaces. Name methods for what they fetch, not how.
rules.why: Leaking an IQueryable/EF shape breaks the abstraction that lets non-IQueryable backends (Dapper, document stores, hand-written SQL) implement the same contract.
rules.check: Look for store interface methods that take or return IQueryable or Expression parameters, or that use generic predicate or specification arguments.

rules.statement: When a reader needs only a few columns, return a lightweight projection type from the store query (a narrow SELECT) instead of the full entity with its child collections. Fetch the full entity only when the caller really needs it.
rules.why: Projections stop the query from joining or materializing unneeded child collections such as settings or secrets.
rules.check: Look for store queries that load full entities with Include()s of child collections when the caller only reads identifiers or a few scalar fields.

rules.statement: When the domain compares a value case-sensitively but the schema stores only a case-folded normalized column, filter on the normalized column in the database as a widening pre-filter, then re-apply the exact case-sensitive match in memory on the returned rows.
rules.why: The normalized filter never drops a true match and stays sargable. The in-memory re-check keeps the case-sensitive semantics the specification requires (for example, RFC 6749 scopes and RFC 8707 resource identifiers).
rules.check: Look for queries that filter on a Normalized* column with no follow-up exact case-sensitive comparison, or case-sensitive values compared only by their normalized form.

rules.statement: Do not add a stateful per-request cache with invalidation in front of a store just to avoid redundant full-set reads. Push the filters into store queries instead, and add a cache on top of those queries only if profiling shows query count is the bottleneck.
rules.why: A cache keeps the fetch-all shape and in-memory filtering, and makes correctness depend on cache freshness and invalidation.
rules.check: Look for new cached collection providers that load a whole store set and filter it in memory.
